title: Redirect rule item (erMatchRule)
$comment: The DynamoDB item shape the Lambda@Edge reads for a redirect (viewer-request). Modeled on EdgeRedirectRule/MatchCondition from the source project's redirect-rule-types.ts.

pk.description: Host, e.g. www.example.com. DynamoDB partition key.

sk.description: REDIRECT#<priority>, priority zero-padded to 5 digits; lower = higher priority; unique per host per type.

redirectURL.description: Where the rule sends the request: an absolute http(s) URL, a root-relative path starting with "/" — and a path means a path on this host, so "//host" and "/\host" are not paths — or a target beginning with a capture reference ("$1/$2/"), whose leading segment only exists once the edge substitutes it. The first two are the console's "Relative URL" toggle, one field in two forms.
redirectURL.$comment:
Whitespace is rejected anywhere and a second "/" or a "\\" cannot follow the first, both because the value is written to a Location header verbatim: a raw CR/LF would split the response, and the browser resolves "//evil.example.com" against the scheme alone, leaving the host entirely. The scheme is spelled as character classes because draft-07 `pattern` has no case-insensitive flag.

The third alternative is a template, not a URL: a target that *starts* with `$n` has no leading segment to check, because the edge builds it from the capture at request time (`rules-service.ts` substitutes `$1` from the first matching regex condition). Whether that expands to something rooted depends on where the condition's group opens, which only the caller can see — the console judges it in `ruleDraft.ts` (`capturesFromRequestStart`), and this pattern deliberately stops short of guessing. What it still refuses is `$n` followed by "//" or "/\\": an unfilled group substitutes as the empty string, so those expand to the off-host case above.

disabled.$comment: Optional; absent means enabled. The Lambda@Edge filters out rules where disabled=true (RulesService.loadRules), so a toggle takes effect within the edge cache TTL (~1 min). The console writes it through PATCH.

if.$comment: The if/then: a redirect with a `country` condition may not also have a `header`, `cookie` or `protocol` one. Such a redirect is evaluated at origin-request (the country only exists from there on), where the request holds only the headers and cookies the behavior's policies forward. A dropped one reads as "" — indistinguishable from a viewer who never sent it — and a negated condition then matches everyone. `protocol` for the same reason: the edge reads it from `X-Forwarded-Proto`, which CloudFront does not guarantee at origin-request, and falls back to "https" without it. Not applied to rewrites: they always ran at origin-request, so their header and cookie conditions already depended on the policies. See infra/lambda/README.md#what-a-geo-redirect-cannot-read.

match.$comment: Shared match condition, referenced by rewrite-rule.schema.json. Field names/enums mirror MatchCondition + MatchType/MatchOperator in redirect-rule-types.ts.

matchValue.$comment: Space-separated alternatives, Akamai-style: any variant may match (RulesService.evaluateMatch splits on " "). Documented here because it is the whole mechanism a `country` condition uses to mean "is one of" — see the conditional below.

headerName.description: Required when matchType is "header"; disallowed otherwise.

allOf.$comment: headerName is required iff matchType is "header".

A country condition carries ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, space-separated, and is a set membership test — so the operator can only be `equals`, which the space-splitting above turns into "is one of". The pattern validates the format and deliberately not the list of countries: CloudFront publishes no such list, its geolocation database changes without notice, and a closed enum here would reject a legitimate new country until the schema shipped again. Same reasoning as getAllowedRegions in console/api/src/lib/aws-regions.ts. `required` so an item missing matchType fails on that alone, without a confusing second error about matchValue's format.
